notes:
Lyriix Android v0.2.11

- Lyriix can be selected as your phone's default digital assistant. The headphone assistant gesture can open a small music-command screen directly, without starting Perplexity or loading the full library screen. In Settings, use Headphone voice controls to choose the assistant and test voice input. JBL users should use their phone/native assistant option where available.
- Voice controls now use the speech recognition API directly and prefer on-device recognition on supported phones. Short skip, next, previous, and pause commands can act on partial recognition after a brief 120 ms stability check; final recognition cannot execute the same command twice. Song requests wait for a complete recognition result so partial titles do not start the wrong song.
- Exact song titles play directly even when several songs share the same title. A downloaded exact match is preferred, followed by an available exact match in library order. Adding the artist with "by" narrows the match. Only unclear, non-exact matches open the search results.
- The music catalog is prepared while you speak. Playing a requested song reuses its existing queue entry or inserts just that song, preserving Up Next instead of rebuilding a full playback queue or search screen.
- Added a one-time microphone permission for direct listening and temporary headset audio routing on Android 12 and newer. Closing voice controls releases the microphone and route; cancelling or recognition failure resumes the same song when appropriate. Typed commands remain available without microphone access. No paid voice API or continuous background listening is used.
- Speech-provider availability, language models, Bluetooth microphone setup, streaming, and locked-screen behavior can affect response time. Instant recognition is not guaranteed. Pixel 10 / JBL Live 660NC physical-device behavior still needs user testing.
- Existing music, themes, pairing, accounts, and permanent Android update signing remain compatible.
